title: Newgen Software Technologies Ltd - 540900 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Newgen Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.4% to INR422 crore, with H1 up 8.8% to INR779 crore; license revenue fell 19.2% YoY against a high base.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 5.4% YoY to INR422 crore and H1 grew 8.8% to INR779 crore, led by EMEA (+19.4%) and US (+17.1%), while India (-12.6%) and APAC (-6.4%) declined. EBITDA rose 6.5% to INR109 crore with a 25.8% margin, and PAT rose 6.3% to INR87 crore (20.6% margin). Subscription revenue overtook license revenue during the quarter, and management attributed the license decline to deal closure timing rather than weaker demand. Management reiterated double-digit FY27 growth, which implies a stronger H2 than H1's roughly 8%.

financial_highlights.metric: Net receivables / net DSO (end Sep quarter)

segments.name: EMEA
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.4% YoY, recovering with normalised travel and demand for enterprise automation and industry offerings. Management cites strong license performance here.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 17.1% YoY on higher subscription sales and market penetration; healthcare lines (provider lifecycle, contract management, complaints and grievances) gained traction.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue declined 12.6% YoY; management says three or four large RFPs slipped from earlier and NBFC deals skipped Q2, expected to close in Q3.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: Revenue declined about 6.4% YoY, which management attributes to timing and execution variability.

segments.name: Recurring revenue streams
segments.commentary: SaaS grew 36.4%, support 10.3%, ATS 7.9%; annuity revenue grew 15%. Subscription revenue surpassed license revenue in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit FY27 revenue growth targeted; management says H1 growth of about 7.7-7.8% is depressed by a high Q2 FY26 base (about INR70-plus crore license revenue).
Management expects Q3 and Q4 to accelerate on license and other lines, plus subscription revenue from large H1 SaaS deals.
Implementation revenue build-up expected to continue at similar growth in Q3 and Q4.
EBITDA and PAT margin guidance of 20-22% net margin for the year; management expects to maintain or expand margins.
Management expects DSO to improve, mainly from Middle East collections delays, in coming quarters.
Long-term goal to return to the roughly 20% revenue CAGR achieved over the last seven to eight years.
capex_capacity: Product development is around 10-11% of revenue and sales and marketing around 22% of revenue (CFO); management also cited 15-20% of revenue going into product development.
Manpower held roughly flat; management says growth can be delivered with similar headcount through AI engineering and operational efficiencies.
Released NewgenONE AI Studio, Agent Studio 1.0 and Agent Flow 2.0 during the quarter.
Management says AI deals shorten implementation time by 15-20%.
demand_pricing: Nine new logos added in Q2 (vs 15 in the same quarter last year); management says logo count depends on closures in the quarter.
Ten AI-based deal bookings in H1 across banking and financial services and government; AI deal sizes are 20-40% larger where AI components are included.
AI offerings sold on perpetual or subscription license; token and operating costs are borne by the customer and not bundled into deal size.
Partners contribute about 20% of business, unchanged; GSI and Big Four partners are focused on large deals, channel partners on small and mid-size deals.
Banking is slowing as banks run AI POCs in core areas (CASA, lending, trade finance, payments) under harsh regulation; management expects pickup in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is weak license signing a shift toward SaaS, or closure timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said license is up QoQ but down YoY due to closure timing and a higher base; India and EMEA pipelines are healthy and India closures slipped to coming quarters. Demand has not weakened.

qa_highlights.question: Was the implementation revenue jump QoQ driven by one-off milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a special focus on milestone closure for revenue recognition and billing, plus Q1 milestone slippages completed in Q2, drove the QoQ improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 growth accelerate enough to deliver double-digit FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated double-digit growth target, citing large SaaS deals closed in H1 and license pipeline closures to accelerate Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be viewed as AI shifts spend between R&D and execution efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs have been stable for four to six quarters, efficiency gains from AI are being reinvested selectively, and margin is expected to be maintained or expanded.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivables/DSO high?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it mainly to delayed collections from certain customers in the Middle East; steps are being taken and improvement is expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI cannibalise implementation and support revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said support is spread across about 600 customers and AI is mainly an efficiency lever; it framed implementation and support as part of delivering product.

risks_watch: License revenue down 19.2% YoY; H2 double-digit growth depends on Q3 and Q4 license closures, especially India NBFC and large RFP deals.
India (-12.6%) and APAC (-6.4%) declines; management expects a pickup but has not quantified it.
Receivables rose; net DSO of 144 days, with Middle East collection delays cited.
New logo additions dropped to nine from 15 a year earlier; management points to closure timing.
Management did not disclose AI-linked revenue, citing it is still being identified internally.
Banking growth has been slow for a second year; AI-led refresh deals may take time to convert from POC.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and H2 recovery, though defensive on license decline and India/APAC weakness, which management attributes to closure timing. Management was evasive on AI revenue quantification and on the buyback, which is only under Board consideration.
key_quotes: This is not because of the weaker demand. This is mostly because of the closure cycle or that happens in the quarter.
So, I think we believe that even in coming quarters also, we will surely maintain the margin and possibly expand the margin also.
So, we do not have large number of support people in any one or two clients.

growth.why: Management reiterated double-digit FY27 revenue growth, backed by expected Q3/Q4 acceleration in license and subscription revenue, slipped India RFPs expected to close in Q3, and AI deal momentum; no new capacity is being added and the company says growth comes with flat headcount.
